title: Maximally Great Being Definition Proof
description: A structured branching graph exploring the Maximally Great Being Definition Proof, analyzing the distinction between Maximal Excellence and Maximal Greatness, the Evil God symmetry challenge, and attribute coherence.

nodes.title: Maximally Great Being Definition Proof
nodes.summary: Formulated within modal ontological frameworks, Maximal Greatness is defined as possessing Maximal Excellence (omnipotence, omniscience, and moral perfection) in EVERY possible world. If such a concept is coherent and possible in at least one world, S5 modal logic entails that a Maximally Great Being necessarily exists in all possible worlds, including the actual world.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Imagine a superhero who isn't just strong in one video game, but is maxed out at 100% strength, wisdom, and goodness in EVERY video game that could ever be created! Thinkers argue that if such an ultimate champion is even possible in one world, he HAS to exist in real life too!

nodes.title: Plantinga's Distinction: Excellence vs. Greatness
nodes.summary: Alvin Plantinga refines ontological definitions by distinguishing Maximal Excellence (having maximum power, knowledge, and goodness in a given world) from Maximal Greatness (having Maximal Excellence across ALL possible worlds). This converts the ontological argument into a claim about necessary modal properties.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Philosopher Alvin Plantinga made a clever distinction: being awesome in ONE universe is called 'Maximal Excellence', but being awesome in EVERY possible universe is 'Maximal Greatness'! That makes God's power impossible to shut off in any universe.

nodes.title: Stephen Law's Evil God Challenge (Symmetry)
nodes.summary: Philosopher Stephen Law constructs a symmetrical parody: define a Maximally EVIL Being (possessing maximal malice, omnipotence, and omniscience in all possible worlds). The exact same modal logic dictates that if a Maximally Evil Being is possible, it exists in reality. Since neither hypothesis can be ruled out by modal logic alone, the argument overgenerates.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Stephen Law showed a catch: what if we define a 'Maximally Evil Monster' who has maximum cruelty in every single world? The exact same math logic says the Evil Monster must exist! Since both can't be true, the definition trick fails.

nodes.title: Privatio Boni & Moral Asymmetry Response
nodes.summary: Theists respond using the Augustinian 'Privatio Boni' (evil as a privation of good): evil is not an independent positive perfection, but a defect or corruption of good. Thus, 'maximal evil' is a self-contradictory concept (like a highest prime number or total blindness that still sees), whereas maximal goodness is intrinsically coherent.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Theists reply: evil isn't a real positive power—it's just a broken piece of good, like rust on a car! You can't have '100% pure rust without any metal,' so a 'Maximally Evil Monster' is a broken concept that collapses.

nodes.title: Symmetry in Evidential Experience
nodes.summary: Skeptics counter that even if evil is metaphysically privative, our empirical world contains vast amounts of cruelty and suffering, which is just as incompatible with a Maximally Good Being as small acts of love are with a Maximally Evil Being.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Skeptics answer back: even if rust isn't metal, look around! The world has way too much cruelty and suffering for a 100% Good Being, and way too much love for a 100% Evil Being.

nodes.title: Paradoxes of Co-existing Divine Attributes
nodes.summary: Critics argue that combining omnipotence, omniscience, immutability, and supreme moral perfection into a single definition introduces logical contradictions (e.g., can a morally perfect being commit a wicked act? Can an immutable being experience time?). If the attributes are mutually incompatible, 'Maximal Greatness' is impossible.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Critics argue: putting all superpowers into one definition creates rule clashes! Can an all-good God tell a lie? Can a God who never changes hear a new prayer? If the superpowers clash, the definition breaks.

nodes.title: Anselmian Perfect Being Theology Refinements
nodes.summary: Defenders refine divine attributes by defining omnipotence as the ability to do whatever is logically consistent with perfection, and omniscience as knowing all true propositions. By removing anthropomorphic distortions, maximal attributes form a harmonious metaphysical unity.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Defenders fix the rules: omnipotence means doing anything that makes LOGICAL sense, not silly nonsense like drawing a round square! When defined carefully, all divine superpowers fit together like puzzle pieces.

nodes.title: Equating Conceivability with Metaphysical Possibility
nodes.summary: Skeptics contend that the premise 'A Maximally Great Being is possible' relies on mere epistemic conceivability (it doesn't seem immediately contradictory), which does not guarantee genuine metaphysical possibility (like Goldbach's conjecture being true or false).
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Skeptics point out: just because you can picture something in your head without your brain exploding doesn't mean it's ACTUALLY possible in real universe logic!

nodes.title: Presumption of Possibility Standard
nodes.summary: Defenders argue that in philosophy, rational intuition establishes a presumption of possibility for a concept unless an internal logical contradiction is explicitly demonstrated. Since no contradiction in maximal greatness has been proven, its possibility stands.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Defenders argue: in math and logic, an idea is assumed possible UNLESS someone proves it has a secret contradiction. Since no one proved God's superpowers contradict each other, it stays possible!

nodes.title: Reverse Modal Proof of Non-Existence
nodes.summary: Skeptics utilize the exact same S5 modal logic: (1) It is possible that a Maximally Great Being does NOT exist. (2) If it is possible that God does not exist, then God does not exist in at least one possible world. (3) By S5 logic, a necessary being must exist in ALL worlds or NONE. (4) Therefore, God does not exist in any world.
nodes.summary_5th_grader: Atheists flip the exact same logic upside down: if it's even POSSIBLE that God doesn't exist in one universe, then by the rules of logic, God CANNOT exist in any universe at all!
